title: Polished Crystal Gym Leaders: Order, Levels, Teams & Counters
description: Polished Crystal Gym Leader guide with Johto and Kanto order, level caps, teams, badge rewards, strategy notes, and counter recommendations for all 16 leaders.
html:
This guide has not been peer reviewed yet!

The information presented may be incomplete, inaccurate, or represent a single perspective. Please verify critical details independently or join the Discord for community support if needed.

Introduction

Polished Crystal has all 16 Gym Leaders: eight in Johto, then eight in Kanto after the Elite Four. Each section below has the actual team display, threats to plan around, practical counters, badge rewards, and the leader's level range.

Gym order and level guide

RegionLeadersTeam levels
Johto
Falkner → Bugsy → Whitney → Morty → Chuck → Jasmine → Pryce → Clair
10–47
Kanto
Brock → Misty → Lt. Surge → Erika → Janine → Sabrina → Blaine → Blue
56–70

For any individual fight, use the team display in that leader's section rather than assuming vanilla Crystal teams. If you are building around a coming badge, the Team Builder, Type Chart, and each linked Pokémon profile are the useful next stops.

Johto Gym Leaders

Falkner - Violet City

Team Overview

Falkner's team is all Flying-type. His Pokémon range from level 10–13.

Key Pokémon:

  • Natu (Psychic/Flying, Level 10) - Peck, Night Shade, Mud-Slap to lower accuracy
  • Hoothoot (Normal/Flying, Level 11) - Hypnosis to put you to sleep, Confusion
  • Pidgeotto (Normal/Flying, Level 13) - His ace, Roost to heal, holds Pecha Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Flying types are weak to Electric, Rock, and Ice moves. Electric and Rock moves are super effective against his entire team. Watch out for Mud-Slap - it reduces accuracy and gets annoying fast. Pidgeotto can heal itself with Roost, and Hoothoot's Hypnosis will put you to sleep. Bring Awakening items (or just power through)!

AI Behavior: Falkner uses Super Potions and switches Pokémon strategically, targeting opponents with reduced accuracy using Mud-Slap.

Recommended Counters:

  • Geodude/Onix - Rock-type works great against Flying; Rock Throw hits super effectively
  • Mareep/Flaaffy - Electric moves hit all of his team super effectively
  • Gastly - Immune to Normal and Fighting moves
  • Any Pokémon with Thunder Shock, Spark, or Rock Throw

After beating Falkner, you'll receive the Zephyr Badge, which lets Pokémon up to level 20 obey, plus TM51 (Roost).

Bugsy - Azalea Town

Team Overview

Bugsy's team is all Bug-type, mostly with Flying dual-typing. His Pokémon range from level 14–17.

Key Pokémon:

  • Butterfree (Bug/Flying, Level 14) - Sleep Powder and Poison Powder for status, Confusion
  • Beedrill (Bug/Poison, Level 14) - Poison Sting, Fury Strikes
  • Yanma (Bug/Flying, Level 14) - Double Team to raise evasion, Sonic Boom
  • Scyther (Bug/Flying, Level 17) - His ace, very fast with U-Turn and Pursuit

Strategy & Tips:

Bug-types are weak to Fire, Flying, and Rock attacks. Three of his Pokémon are Bug/Flying, making them 4× weak to Rock. Beedrill is Bug/Poison though. Butterfree has both Sleep Powder and Poison Powder. Scyther is fast and powerful but has low Defense.

AI Behavior: Bugsy uses Super Potions and sometimes switches Pokémon. He focuses on inflicting status conditions and uses Double Team to stall.

Recommended Counters:

  • Quilava/Cyndaquil - Fire moves are super effective against all his Pokémon
  • Geodude/Onix - Rock Throw deals 4× damage to Flying-types
  • Pidgeotto - Flying moves are super effective and resist Bug
  • Mareep - Electric moves hit most of his team
  • Any Pokémon with Rock Throw, Ember, or Spark

After defeating Bugsy, you'll get the Hive Badge (allows Cut outside battle) and TM89 (U-Turn).

Whitney - Goldenrod City

Team Overview

Whitney's team features Normal-type Pokémon with some Fairy-type moves. They range from level 19–21.

Key Pokémon:

  • Clefairy (Fairy, Level 19) - Metronome (random move), Disarming Voice, Attract
  • Teddiursa (Normal, Level 20) - Lick to paralyze, Attract, Feint Attack
  • Munchlax (Normal, Level 19) - Defense Curl + Rollout combo
  • Miltank (Normal, Level 21) - Her strongest Pokémon with Scrappy ability, has Defense Curl + Rollout, Fresh Snack for healing, holds Lum Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Normal types are weak to Fighting. Whitney's Miltank is legendary for Defense Curl → Rollout (doubles in power each turn: 30, 60, 120, 240, 480). Fresh Snack heals her, and Lum Berry cures status. Scrappy means Ghost types can't dodge using their immunity. Attract is brutal against male Pokémon, so bring female or genderless ones. Break the Rollout chain by taking Miltank out or making it miss.

AI Behavior: Whitney uses Hyper Potions and occasionally switches Pokémon. She's very aggressive with Defense Curl + Rollout and won't switch when the combo is active.

Recommended Counters:

  • Geodude/Graveler - High Defense helps tank Rollout, can use Magnitude or Rock Throw
  • Machop/Machoke - Fighting-type moves are super effective
  • Heracross - Found on Route 29 using Headbutt, strong Fighting-type
  • Female or Genderless Pokémon - Immune to Attract
  • Status moves - Paralysis, Sleep, or Burn cripple Miltank

After beating Whitney, you'll get the Plain Badge (allows Strength outside battle) and TM45 (Attract).

Morty - Ecruteak City

Team Overview

Morty's team consists of Ghost-type Pokémon and other spooky Pokémon. His team levels range from 24–26.

Key Pokémon:

  • Haunter (Ghost/Poison, Level 24) - Levitate ability, Hypnosis, Ice Punch, Shadow Claw
  • Noctowl (Normal/Flying, Level 24) - Hypnosis, Hex (doubles damage on sleeping targets)
  • Misdreavus (Ghost, Level 25) - Nasty Plot to boost Special Attack, Shadow Ball, Dark Pulse
  • Gengar (Ghost/Poison, Level 26) - His ace with Levitate, Hypnosis + Dream Eater combo, Thunderbolt, holds Wide Lens

Strategy & Tips:

Ghost-types are weak to Ghost and Dark moves. Pure Ghost-types are immune to Normal and Fighting moves, making those types useless here. Levitate on Haunter and Gengar makes them immune to Ground moves too. Hypnosis is super dangerous - Gengar uses Dream Eater to heal while you sleep, and Noctowl's Hex deals double damage to sleeping targets. Bring Awakening items! Misdreavus can boost with Nasty Plot. Dark-types resist Ghost moves and deal super effective damage, making them your best bet.

AI Behavior: Morty relies on Hyper Potions and will switch Pokémon occasionally. He uses sleep-based control strategies, combining Hypnosis + Dream Eater to stall and regain health.

Recommended Counters:

  • Umbreon - Dark-type resists Ghost, Bite is super effective
  • Murkrow - Dark/Flying available before this gym
  • Haunter/Gengar - Ghost moves are super effective
  • Any Pokémon with Bite, Crunch, or Shadow Ball
  • Bring Awakening items - Counter Hypnosis + Dream Eater

Defeating Morty gives you the Fog Badge, which lets you use Surf outside of battle, and TM30 (Shadow Ball)!

Chuck - Cianwood City

Team Overview

Chuck's team consists of Fighting-type Pokémon with some coverage. His team levels range from 28–31.

Key Pokémon:

  • Primeape (Fighting, Level 30) - Defiant ability, Karate Chop, Seismic Toss, Dynamic Punch
  • Farfetch'd Galarian (Fighting, Level 29) - Steadfast ability, Reversal, Body Slam, Swords Dance
  • Hitmontop (Fighting, Level 28) - Intimidate ability, Bulk Up, Sucker Punch, Rapid Spin
  • Poliwrath (Water/Fighting, Level 31) - His ace with Water Absorb, Ice Punch, Hypnosis, Dynamic Punch, holds Zoom Lens

Strategy & Tips:

Fighting-types are weak to Flying, Psychic, and Fairy moves. Dynamic Punch has low accuracy but hits hard and confuses when it connects. Poliwrath is Water/Fighting, making it weak to Flying, Psychic, Fairy, Electric, and Grass. Hitmontop's Intimidate lowers your Attack. Primeape's Defiant ability raises its Attack if its stats are lowered.

AI Behavior: Chuck uses Full Heals to cure status and may switch Pokémon. His strategy is aggressive, using high-risk, high-reward moves like Dynamic Punch.

Recommended Counters:

  • Pidgeot/Crobat - Flying-types resist Fighting and hit super effectively
  • Espeon/Alakazam - Psychic-types dominate Fighting-types
  • Any Pokémon with Psychic, Flying, or Aerial Ace
  • Grass or Electric - Super effective against Poliwrath

After defeating Chuck, you'll get the Storm Badge, which allows Fly outside of battle, and TM01 (Focus Punch).

Jasmine - Olivine City

Team Overview

Jasmine's team is all Steel-type with a focus on Defense. Her team levels range from 33–37.

Key Pokémon:

  • Skarmory (Steel/Flying, Level 34) - Mud-Slap, Drill Peck, Spikes, Steel Wing
  • Magneton (Electric/Steel, Level 33) - Thunder Wave, Thunderbolt, Tri Attack
  • Forretress (Bug/Steel, Level 34) - Spikes, Gyro Ball, Defense Curl + Rollout
  • Scizor (Bug/Steel, Level 33) - Pursuit, Aerial Ace, Metal Claw, Slash
  • Steelix (Steel/Ground, Level 37) - Her ace, Body Slam, Screech, Rock Slide, Iron Tail, holds Leftovers

Strategy & Tips:

Steel-types are weak to Fire, Fighting, and Ground moves. Jasmine's team has high Defense but lower Special Defense - use special attackers. Steelix (Steel/Ground) is 2× weak to Water, Fire, Fighting, and Ground moves, and immune to Electric. Watch out for Spikes from Skarmory and Forretress. Iron Tail can lower Defense. Magneton is 4× weak to Ground and 2× weak to Fire.

AI Behavior: Jasmine uses Max Potions and will sometimes switch Pokémon. She plays defensively, setting up Spikes early and stalling with high-Defense Pokémon.

Recommended Counters:

  • Typhlosion/Magmar - Fire moves are super effective
  • Graveler/Golem - Ground moves deal heavy damage
  • Machamp - Fighting moves are super effective
  • Feraligatr - Water moves hit Steelix super effectively

After Jasmine is defeated, you'll obtain the Mineral Badge and TM23 (Iron Tail).

Pryce - Mahogany Town

Team Overview

Pryce's team is pure Ice-type with a few dual-types. His Pokémon range from level 38–42.

Key Pokémon:

  • Dewgong (Water/Ice, Level 39) - Rain Dance, Waterfall, Aurora Beam, Rest, holds Chesto Berry
  • Sneasel (Dark/Ice, Level 38) - Swords Dance, Icicle Crash, Screech, Slash
  • Cloyster (Water/Ice, Level 38) - Defense Curl, Supersonic, Water Pulse, Ice Shard
  • Lapras (Water/Ice, Level 40) - Sing, Confuse Ray, Ancient Power, Ice Beam
  • Mamoswine (Ice/Ground, Level 42) - His ace, Magnitude, Ancient Power, Avalanche, Fury Strikes, holds Sitrus Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Ice-types are weak to Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel moves. Most of Pryce's team is dual Water/Ice, making Electric and Rock moves effective. Mamoswine is Ice/Ground, making it weak to Water, Grass, Fire, Fighting, and Steel. Watch out for Lapras's Sing and Rain Dance boosting Water moves. Dewgong's Rest + Chesto Berry combo restores full HP. Sneasel is fast and dangerous after Swords Dance.

AI Behavior: Pryce relies on Max Potions and will occasionally switch Pokémon. He tries to control battle pace with weather conditions and sleep.

Recommended Counters:

  • Typhlosion - Fire-type destroys Ice
  • Machamp - Fighting moves are super effective
  • Feraligatr - Water moves are super effective against Mamoswine
  • Electric-types - Hit Water/Ice Pokémon hard
  • Rock or Steel-types - Resist Ice and hit super effectively

After defeating Pryce, you'll get the Glacier Badge, which lets you use Headbutt outside of battle, and TM16 (Icy Wind).

Clair - Blackthorn City

Team Overview

Clair has a team of Dragon-type and Dragon-like Pokémon. Her Pokémon range from level 43–47.

Key Pokémon:

  • Gyarados (Water/Flying, Level 43) - Crunch, Thrash, Dragon Pulse, Aqua Tail
  • Yanmega (Bug/Flying, Level 45) - Double Team, Supersonic, Ancient Power, Dragon Pulse
  • Ampharos (Electric, Level 44) - Thunder Wave, Confuse Ray, Thunderbolt, Dragon Pulse
  • Dragonair (Dragon, Level 44) - Thunder Wave, Thunderbolt, Ice Beam, Dragon Pulse
  • Kingdra (Water/Dragon, Level 47) - Her ace with Sniper ability, Smokescreen, Hyper Beam, Dragon Pulse, Surf, holds Shell Bell

Strategy & Tips:

Dragon-types are weak to Ice, Dragon, and Fairy attacks. However, Kingdra is only weak to Dragon and Fairy, making Ice attacks useless against it. Several Pokémon use Thunder Wave - be prepared for paralysis. Dragonair uses Ice Beam for coverage. Gyarados is 4× weak to Electric attacks. Yanmega uses Double Team to raise evasion. Ampharos isn't Dragon-type but uses Dragon Pulse.

AI Behavior: Clair uses Full Heals and Max Potions, making her well-equipped for long fights. She switches Pokémon frequently and loves to spam Thunder Wave to slow your team down.

Recommended Counters:

  • Ice Beam users - Super effective against most Dragons
  • Electric-types - Hit Gyarados hard (4×); Kingdra resists Electric via Dragon typing
  • Dragonite - Dragon moves are super effective
  • Fairy-types - Immune to Dragon moves, super effective against Dragons
  • Jolteon/Ampharos - Fast Electric-types

After defeating Clair, you'll get the Rising Badge, which lets you use Waterfall outside of battle, and TM24 (Dragon Breath).

Kanto Gym Leaders

Brock - Pewter City

Team Overview

Brock's team has Rock-type Pokémon and Fossils. His Pokémon range from level 63–68.

Key Pokémon:

  • Golem (Rock/Ground, Level 64) - Defense Curl + Rollout combo, Rock Slide, Earthquake
  • Rhydon (Rock/Ground, Level 63) - Avalanche, Rock Slide, Earthquake, Outrage, holds Eviolite
  • Omastar (Rock/Water, Level 65) - Ancient Power, Surf, Protect, Spikes
  • Onix (Rock/Ground, Level 68) - Iron Tail, Rock Slide, Earthquake, Sandstorm
  • Kabutops (Rock/Water, Level 65) - Slash, Surf, Endure, Giga Drain
  • Aerodactyl (Rock/Flying, Level 65) - Aerial Ace, Supersonic, Ancient Power, Hyper Beam

Strategy & Tips:

Rock-types are weak to Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, and Steel attacks. Brock's Pokémon have high Defense but lower Special Defense - special attackers work best. Water moves are 4× effective on Golem, Rhydon, and Onix. Kabutops and Omastar are part Water and weak to Electric and Grass. Many Pokémon have Earthquake. Omastar uses Spikes.

AI Behavior: Brock uses Full Heals and Max Potions and occasionally switches Pokémon. He employs a defensive grind strategy with Spikes and Rollout sweep attacks.

Recommended Counters:

  • Feraligatr/Blastoise - Water moves are 4× effective against Golem, Rhydon, and Onix
  • Meganium/Venusaur - Grass moves hit hard
  • Machamp - Fighting moves are super effective
  • Surf or Earthquake users - Cover most of his team

Once you defeat Brock, you'll receive the Boulder Badge and TM48 (Rock Slide)!

Misty - Cerulean City

Team Overview

Misty's team features Water-type Pokémon with various coverage types. They range from level 60–64.

Key Pokémon:

  • Golduck (Water/Psychic, Level 61) - Water Pulse, Disable, Calm Mind, Psychic
  • Quagsire (Water/Ground, Level 60) - Scald, Calm Mind, Earthquake, Rain Dance
  • Lapras (Water/Ice, Level 62) - Surf, Perish Song, Blizzard, Rain Dance
  • Kingler (Water, Level 60) - Defense Curl, Stomp, Protect, Crabhammer
  • Lanturn (Water/Electric, Level 62) - Water Pulse, Thunderbolt, Ice Beam, Recover
  • Starmie (Water/Psychic, Level 64) - Her ace, Scald, Confuse Ray, Recover, Ice Beam, holds Sitrus Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Water-types are weak to Electric and Grass moves. Misty uses Calm Mind to build momentum and Rain Dance, then follows with powerful Water moves. Quagsire is immune to Electric but 4× weak to Grass. Lanturn is Water/Electric and weak to Ground and Grass. Starmie can heal with Recover and has high Speed. Watch out for boosted Water moves when she uses Rain Dance. Lapras is bulky and uses Perish Song.

AI Behavior: Misty uses Full Heals and Max Potions, and switches Pokémon frequently. She likes to set up with Calm Mind and Rain Dance.

Recommended Counters:

  • Ampharos/Raikou - Electric moves hit most of her team
  • Meganium - Grass-type hits all Pokémon super effectively
  • Jolteon - Fast Electric-type
  • Grass and Electric Pokémon - Double coverage

After beating Misty, you'll get the Cascade Badge and TM63 (Water Pulse).

Lt. Surge - Vermilion City

Team Overview

Lt. Surge's team consists of Electric-type Pokémon. His team levels range from 56–60.

Key Pokémon:

  • Electabuzz (Electric, Level 58) - Quick Attack, Thunder Punch, Light Screen, Wild Charge, holds Eviolite
  • Electrode (Electric, Level 56) - Screech, Double Team, Thunderbolt, Explosion
  • Magnezone (Electric/Steel, Level 57) - Light Screen, Double Team, Wild Charge, Zap Cannon
  • Electrode (Electric, Level 56) - Screech, Double Team, Wild Charge, Explosion (second one)
  • Jolteon (Electric, Level 58) - Wild Charge, Thunder Wave, Agility, Thunder
  • Raichu (Electric, Level 60) - His ace, Thunder Wave, Quick Attack, Wild Charge, Thunder, holds Sitrus Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Electric-types are weak to Ground-type attacks. Ground-types are immune to Electric attacks, making them ideal opponents. Be cautious of Magnezone - it's resistant to many attacks and carries Zap Cannon. Both Electrodes can use Explosion. Lt. Surge puts up Light Screen to reduce damage. Jolteon and Raichu are fast Pokémon.

AI Behavior: Lt. Surge uses Full Heals, Max Potions, and may switch Pokémon. He uses Light Screen to reduce special damage and might use Explosion if cornered.

Recommended Counters:

  • Any Ground-type - Immune to Electric moves and deal super effective damage
  • Donphan/Rhyperior - High Attack Ground-types
  • Steelix - Resists Electric, hits super effectively
  • Earthquake users - One-shot most of his team

Once you've defeated Lt. Surge, you'll get the Thunder Badge and TM57 (Wild Charge).

Erika - Celadon City

Team Overview

Erika's team features Grass-type Pokémon with support from Sunny Day. Her Pokémon range from level 61–65.

Key Pokémon:

  • Sunflora (Grass, Level 61) - Sunny Day, Healing Light, Giga Drain, Flamethrower
  • Tangela (Grass, Level 62) - Growth, Healing Light, Giga Drain, Sleep Powder, holds Eviolite
  • Politoed (Water, Level 61) - Giga Drain, Scald, Ice Beam, Focus Blast (in Polished mode)
  • Victreebel (Grass/Poison, Level 64) - Sunny Day, Healing Light, Acid, Razor Leaf
  • Vileplume (Grass/Poison, Level 65) - Sunny Day, Healing Light, Petal Dance, Solar Beam
  • Bellossom (Grass, Level 65) - Her ace, Sunny Day, Healing Light, Petal Dance, Solar Beam, holds Sitrus Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Grass Pokémon are weak to Fire, Ice, Poison, Flying, and Bug moves. Erika's team uses Sunny Day, which increases Fire moves by 50% and removes Solar Beam's charge turn. Watch out for Sleep Powder and healing moves. In Faithful Mode, Parasect replaces Politoed in this slot.

AI Behavior: Erika uses Full Heals, Max Potions, and sometimes switches. She relies on Sunny Day to power up her strategy.

Recommended Counters:

  • Typhlosion/Charizard - Fire moves destroy Grass, boosted by sun
  • Crobat - Poison/Flying hits super effectively, immune to Ground
  • Pidgeot - Flying moves are super effective
  • Any Fire, Ice, or Flying Pokémon

Once you've defeated Erika, you'll get the Rainbow Badge and TM19 (Giga Drain)!

Janine - Fuchsia City

Team Overview

Janine's team features Poison-type Pokémon with a status focus. Her Pokémon range from level 61–66.

Key Pokémon:

  • Crobat (Poison/Flying, Level 64) - Screech, Toxic, Confuse Ray, Aerial Ace
  • Ariados (Bug/Poison, Level 61) - Agility, Poison Jab, Mean Look, Psychic
  • Qwilfish (Water/Poison, Level 62) - Aqua Tail, Poison Jab, Spikes, Minimize
  • Nidoqueen (Poison/Ground, Level 64) - Toxic, Healing Light, Sludge Bomb, Ice Beam
  • Weezing (Poison, Level 63) - Sludge Bomb, Thunder, Fire Blast, Explosion
  • Venomoth (Bug/Poison, Level 66) - Her ace, Sludge Bomb, Double Team, Gust, Psychic, holds Sitrus Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Poison-types are weak to Ground and Psychic attacks. Janine relies on attrition with Toxic and evasive maneuvers, rarely switching once her strategy starts. Steel-types are immune to Toxic. Crobat is extremely fast. Weezing can use Explosion. Nidoqueen (Poison/Ground) has different weaknesses (Water, Psychic, Ice, Ground). Watch out for Double Team and Minimize.

AI Behavior: Janine uses Full Heals, Max Potions, and will sometimes switch. She relies on Toxic and evasion tactics.

Recommended Counters:

  • Espeon/Alakazam - Psychic moves are super effective
  • Earthquake users - Hit most Pokémon super effectively
  • Steel-types - Immune to Toxic and resist Poison
  • Ground or Psychic Pokémon

Once you've defeated Janine, you'll get the Marsh Badge and TM66 (Poison Jab).

Sabrina - Saffron City

Team Overview

Sabrina uses Psychic-type Pokémon ranging from level 58–62.

Key Pokémon:

  • Espeon (Psychic, Level 61) - Mud-Slap, Quick Attack, Swift, Psychic
  • Girafarig (Normal/Psychic, Level 59) - Psychic, Crunch, Agility, Calm Mind (in Polished mode becomes Farigiraf)
  • Mr. Mime (Psychic/Fairy, Level 60) - Barrier, Reflect, Baton Pass, Psychic
  • Hypno (Psychic, Level 59) - Hypnosis, Dream Eater, Nasty Plot, Psychic
  • Wobbuffet (Psychic, Level 58) - Counter, Mirror Coat, Safeguard, Destiny Bond
  • Alakazam (Psychic, Level 62) - Her ace, Recover, Future Sight, Psychic, Reflect, holds Sitrus Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Psychic-types are weak to Bug, Ghost, and Dark moves. Dark-types are immune to Psychic. Her Pokémon have high Special Attack and Speed. Wobbuffet uses Counter and Mirror Coat defensively. Watch out for Hypnosis followed by Dream Eater. Mr. Mime uses Baton Pass to transfer stat boosts.

AI Behavior: Sabrina uses Full Heals, Max Potions, and switches. She employs Calm Mind and Nasty Plot sweepers, plus Baton Pass from Mr. Mime.

Recommended Counters:

  • Umbreon/Houndoom/Tyranitar - Dark-types immune to Psychic moves
  • Scizor - Bug/Steel resists Psychic, Bug moves super effective
  • Gengar - Ghost-type with Shadow Ball
  • Any Pokémon with Crunch, Bite, or Shadow Ball

Upon defeating Sabrina, you'll receive the Soul Badge and TM29 (Psychic).

Blaine - Cinnabar Island

Team Overview

Blaine's team is all Fire-type Pokémon ranging from level 65–69.

Key Pokémon:

  • Magcargo (Fire/Rock, Level 65) - Curse, Will-O-Wisp, Flamethrower, Rock Slide
  • Magmar (Fire, Level 68) - Sunny Day, Thunder Punch, Flamethrower, Focus Blast, holds Eviolite
  • Arcanine (Fire, Level 66) - Crunch, Flame Charge, Flare Blitz, Take Down
  • Ninetales (Fire, Level 66) - Confuse Ray, Fire Spin, Flamethrower, Will-O-Wisp
  • Flareon (Fire, Level 65) - Will-O-Wisp, Flare Blitz, Quick Attack, Fire Blast
  • Rapidash (Fire, Level 69) - His ace, Quick Attack, Fire Spin, Play Rough, Fire Blast, holds Sitrus Berry

Strategy & Tips:

Fire-types are weak to Water, Ground, and Rock attacks. Blaine uses Sunny Day to boost Fire attacks and Will-O-Wisp to weaken physical attackers. Magcargo (Fire/Rock) is 4× weak to Water and Ground. Many Pokémon have high Speed.

AI Behavior: Blaine uses Full Heals and Max Potions, possibly switching. He boosts Fire power with Sunny Day.

Recommended Counters:

  • Feraligatr/Blastoise - Water-types resist Fire and hit super effectively
  • Golem/Rhyperior - Rock/Ground deals 4× damage to Magcargo
  • Starmie - Fast Water-type
  • Surf or Earthquake users - Cover his entire team

After beating Blaine, you'll get the Volcano Badge and TM61 (Will-O-Wisp)!

Blue - Viridian City

Team Overview

Blue's team doesn't have a specific type specialty - it's diverse. His Pokémon range from level 66–70.

Key Pokémon:

  • Exeggutor (Grass/Psychic, Level 68) - Psychic, Leech Seed, Trick Room, Giga Drain, holds Room Service
  • Umbreon (Dark, Level 69) - Confuse Ray, Toxic, Feint Attack, Protect, holds Leftovers
  • Machamp (Fighting, Level 66) - Dynamic Punch, Earthquake, Stone Edge, Thunder Punch, holds Black Belt
  • Kabutops (Rock/Water, Level 67) - Slash, Surf, Stone Edge, Giga Drain, holds Hard Stone
  • Arcanine (Fire, Level 68) - Roar, Flame Charge, Flamethrower, Extreme Speed, holds Charcoal
  • Blastoise (Water, Level 70) - His ace, Surf, Ice Beam, Body Slam, Flash Cannon, holds Mystic Water

Strategy & Tips:

Blue uses Full Heals and Full Restores, making him very hard to wear down. He switches frequently and adapts strategies based on your team. His use of Trick Room and stalling makes things complex. You can't counter a specific type - you need a balanced team with good coverage. His Pokémon are all high-level with varied movesets. Umbreon stalls with Toxic, Machamp uses low-accuracy Dynamic Punch, and Exeggutor sets up Trick Room. This is the toughest Gym Leader battle.

AI Behavior: Blue adapts constantly, switching to favorable matchups and using items liberally.

Recommended Counters:

  • Balanced team - Cover Water, Fire, Fighting, Grass, Dark, Rock types
  • Electric-types - Hit Blastoise and Kabutops
  • Fighting/Fairy - For Umbreon
  • Ice/Flying - For Exeggutor
  • Full Restores and Revives - This is a long, tough battle

Defeating Blue will earn you the Earth Badge and TM71 (Stone Edge).

General Tips

Before Each Gym Battle

  • Check type matchups - Know what types the Gym Leader uses and bring counters
  • Stock up on items - Potions, Full Heals, and Revives can save a run
  • Level up your team - Being 3-5 levels above the Gym Leader helps significantly
  • Save before battling - Always save so you can retry if needed

During The Battle

  • Use super effective moves - They deal 2× and 4× damage
  • Watch out for setup moves - If a Leader boosts stats, switch or play around it
  • Manage status conditions - Paralysis, sleep, and poison can cripple your team
  • Don't be afraid to switch - Sometimes it's better to switch to resist an attack than to stay in

After Winning

  • Collect your TM - Each Gym Leader gives you a useful TM
  • Plan for the next badge - Think about what types are coming up
  • Register rematches - After beating the Elite Four, you can rematch any Gym Leader for experience and money!

Badge Benefits

Each badge you earn provides benefits beyond just allowing you to progress:

Obedience Levels

Badges increase the level at which traded Pokémon will obey you:

  • 1 Badge - Pokémon up to level 20 obey
  • 2 Badges - Pokémon up to level 30 obey
  • 3 Badges - Pokémon up to level 40 obey
  • 4 Badges - Pokémon up to level 50 obey
  • 5 Badges - Pokémon up to level 60 obey
  • 6 Badges - Pokémon up to level 70 obey
  • 7 Badges - Pokémon up to level 80 obey
  • 8 Badges - All Pokémon obey

HM Usage

Certain badges allow you to use HM moves outside of battle:

  • Zephyr Badge (Falkner) - Use Flash outside battle
  • Hive Badge (Bugsy) - Use Cut outside battle
  • Plain Badge (Whitney) - Use Strength outside battle
  • Fog Badge (Morty) - Use Surf outside battle
  • Storm Badge (Chuck) - Use Fly outside battle
  • Mineral Badge (Jasmine) - Use Whirlpool outside battle
  • Glacier Badge (Pryce) - Use Headbutt outside battle
  • Rising Badge (Clair) - Use Waterfall outside battle
